title: Oh also did I mention they now have a 19 PIECE ORCHESTRA???? #Titaniq...
transcript: Let's talk about all of the Broadway upgrades for Titanique, as this Titanic parody musical, which started at a small off off Broadway theatre, is now playing one of the largest theatres on Broadway. And I'm happy to report that they did very much scale this up for Broadway. They got a brand new set which leans more into, like, the concert aesthetic rather than a more traditional ship set. Off Broadway, they jokingly refer to it as the set of Anything Goes. Now they jokingly refer to it as the set of The Voice. And I do think this set works better in the larger space. All of the costumes got upgrades as well, including a full beauty and the Beast homage during Tale as old as time. And while obviously I was front row, so I can't speak to the view from the back mezz, I thought they did a really good job at scaling it up to fit this ginormous theatre. I also think the show is as funny as it's ever been. It is mostly the same show that was off Broadway with a couple of new bits here and there. They do still have the improv sections, which will change from night to night. And I thought all of the actors were great, including, by the way, Jim Parsons, who I was very skeptical when they announced his casting, but I was actually very pleasantly surprised. At one point, and I kid you not, he says, how's This for a big Bang Theory and then farts in a violinist's face. But the other new cast members are fantastic as well. Melissa Barrera is a freaking star and I really hope she does more musical theatre after this because she has an amazing voice. Deborah Cox as unsinkable Molly Brown also, unsurprisingly, amazing vocalist. She actually got a much deserved mid show standing ovation for all by myself. And Layton Williams, who actually won an Olivier for this role in London, killed me as the iceberg. The rest of the cast is also doing fantastic work reprising roles that they played off Broadway. But I have to give special shout out to Marla Mindelle, who continues to be a tour de force as Celine Dion. When I say I genuinely believe she is front runner for Best Actress in a musical at the Tonys this year, I am not kidding. I think ultimately, if you saw the show off Broadway and liked it, you're gonna like it on Broadway as well. And if you've never seen Titanique before, I don't know that there's ever been a better time.
classificationReason: Creator explicitly attended ('I was front row') and reviews the Broadway transfer's new set, costumes, cast including Jim Parsons, and how the show scaled up from Off-Broadway.
